newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson's house goes up for sale.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson's house goes up for sale.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's house is up for sale at nearly $4 million -- but you need an appointment just to view the mansion where the former football star said he was chipping golf balls the night his ex-wife was murdered.
According to real estate agent Fred Sands, the house at 360 North Rockingham Avenue in the upscale Los Angeles section of Brentwood has six bedrooms, plus a maid's room and 7 1/2 bathrooms.
The house is big enough to entertain 300 people -- something Simpson did after he was acquitted in October 1995 of murdering his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman.

However, the ex-football star was later found liable in civil court for the deaths and ordered to pay $33.5 million in damages to the victims' families. As a result of the award against him, Simpson fell $86,000 behind in mortgage payments and last month, Hawthorne Savings and Loan, which owned the mortgage, put the property up for public auction.
Hawthorne itself bought the house, with its tennis courts, natural rock swimming pool and waterfall slide, for $2.6 million.
Hoping to turn a tidy profit, Hawthorne has handed the sale to Fred Sands Estates at an asking price of $3.95 million.

"This is very prime property and we plan on showing it this week," Sands told Reuters, saying he had received many inquiries about it even before it was listed. "But it is a house which has had (negative) exposure."

Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman were slashed to death outside the former Mrs. Simpson's condominium some two miles (3 km) away, but police testified they found blood drops at Simpson's Rockingham estate and also a bloody glove that matched one found at the murder scene.

However, during the criminal trial, defence attorneys contended the blood and glove were planted by police as part of a conspiracy against Simpson. The mostly black jury found him not guilty in a verdict that split America along largely racial lines.
Because of its notoriety, Sands said ads for the house only mention the address and do not include the usual flattering photograph of the property.

"Viewing is by appointment only, so that someone off the street will not be able to just come in to look around. We have to either know the potential buyer or they must have a letter from their banker," he said.
For $3.95 million, the buyer will get a "lovely home" about 30 years old that Sands said has had extensive updating. There is a large family room, a billiard room and a circular driveway.
However, it is not clear when the new owners will be able to move in, since Simpson still lives there with his two children. He is looking for a rental home in the area.
Sands said there was an agreement "between the bank and the occupant" specifying when Simpson would move out.
"All I can say is it is in the near future," Sands said.
